meta_title: Integral of root tan x: NCERT Exemplar Q43 Solved
meta_desc: Solve the integral of root tan x (NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Q43) using t squared = tan x, then split into standard forms. Free 8-question quiz included.

quiz.title: Integral of Root Tan x Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the substitution t squared = tan x and integrating rational functions with 1 + t to the fourth. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: In ∫ √(tan x) dx, we set t² = tan x. What is dx in terms of t and dt?
questions.explanation: Differentiating t² = tan x gives 2t dt = sec²x dx = (1 + tan²x) dx = (1 + t⁴) dx, so dx = 2t/(1 + t⁴) dt.

questions.q: After the substitution t² = tan x, the integral ∫ √(tan x) dx becomes which of these?
questions.explanation: √(tan x) = t and dx = 2t/(1 + t⁴) dt, so the integrand is t × 2t/(1 + t⁴) = 2t²/(1 + t⁴).

questions.q: To split 2t²/(1 + t⁴), it helps to divide numerator and denominator by t². What does the denominator 1 + t⁴ become?
questions.explanation: Dividing 1 + t⁴ by t² gives 1/t² + t², i.e. t² + 1/t². The numerator 2t² becomes 2.

questions.q: We write 2t²/(1 + t⁴) as the sum of (t² + 1)/(t⁴ + 1) and (t² − 1)/(t⁴ + 1) after multiplying by a constant. What constant works?
questions.explanation: (t² + 1) + (t² − 1) = 2t², so 2t²/(1 + t⁴) = (t² + 1)/(1 + t⁴) + (t² − 1)/(1 + t⁴) directly, with constant 1.

questions.q: For ∫ (t² + 1)/(t⁴ + 1) dt, divide top and bottom by t² and use the substitution u = t − 1/t. What is du?
questions.explanation: d/dt (t − 1/t) = 1 + 1/t². The numerator (t² + 1)/t² = 1 + 1/t² matches du exactly, and t² + 1/t² = u² + 2.

questions.q: For ∫ (t² − 1)/(t⁴ + 1) dt, divide by t² and use v = t + 1/t. The denominator t² + 1/t² equals which expression in v?
questions.explanation: v = t + 1/t gives v² = t² + 2 + 1/t², so t² + 1/t² = v² − 2. And dv = (1 − 1/t²) dt matches the numerator.

questions.q: ∫ du/(u² + 2), where u = t − 1/t, evaluates to which standard form?
questions.explanation: ∫ du/(u² + a²) = (1/a) tan⁻¹(u/a) + C. Here a² = 2, so a = √2, giving (1/√2) tan⁻¹(u/√2) + C.

questions.q: ∫ dv/(v² − 2), where v = t + 1/t, evaluates to which standard form?
questions.explanation: ∫ dv/(v² − a²) = (1/2a) ln|(v − a)/(v + a)| + C. With a = √2 this gives (1/2√2) ln|(v − √2)/(v + √2)| + C.

faq.q: Why substitute t² = tan x instead of t = tan x?
faq.a: The integrand carries a square root, √(tan x). Setting t² = tan x makes √(tan x) equal to t, a clean polynomial in t, so the whole integral turns into a rational function of t with no surd left to fight.

faq.q: Where does the denominator 1 + t⁴ come from?
faq.a: From dx. Differentiating t² = tan x gives 2t dt = sec²x dx = (1 + tan²x) dx = (1 + t⁴) dx. So dx = 2t/(1 + t⁴) dt, and that 1 + t⁴ is what forces the split-into-standard-forms trick.

faq.q: Why split 2t²/(1 + t⁴) into two fractions?
faq.a: A single integral with 1 + t⁴ on the bottom has no direct formula. Writing it as (t² + 1)/(1 + t⁴) + (t² − 1)/(1 + t⁴) lets each piece be reduced by u = t − 1/t and v = t + 1/t into the standard 1/(u² + a²) and 1/(v² − a²) forms.

faq.q: What is the final answer to ∫ √(tan x) dx?
faq.a: Adding the two pieces and putting t = √(tan x): the result is (1/√2) tan⁻¹((tan x − 1)/(√2 · √(tan x))) + (1/2√2) ln|(tan x + 1 − √(2 tan x))/(tan x + 1 + √(2 tan x))| + C.
